provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after ut and none after adventum; 1962 sets both; 1862 closes the petition with a full stop before Qui tecum; 1962 sets a colon (mereamur:); 1862's conclusion cue is the shorter 'Qui tecum vivit,'; 1962 prints 'Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.'; 1862 prints ejus, 1962 prints eius (the project's j orthography restores ejus, so the target text above agrees with the 1862 here by convention rather than by the target's letterforms); OCR noise only: 'TlXcita / Jjj' for the ornamental E at 13537-13538, 'prseparaudas' at 13538. Corroboration: Venice 1570 (degraded-latin; the edition's own record forbids resting a claim or a negative on a raw search over it, so this is corroboration only and nothing here rests on it) at text-layer lines 6091-6098: 'Excita domine corda nostra ad preparandas unigeniti tui vias: vt per eius aduentum, purificatis tibi mentibus seruire mereamur. Qui tecum viuit...' -- note the 1570 sets a comma after adventum but none after ut, so the three witnesses point this clause three different ways.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Excita, Domine, corda nostra ad praeparandas Unigeniti tui vias: ut, per
ejus adventum, purificatis tibi mentibus servire mereamur: Qui tecum vivit
et regnat in unitate.
